item.title: WATCH: Breaking down the best holiday movies
item.description: Andscape senior entertainment reporter Kelley Carter discusses what defines a classic holiday film, shares her top picks and weighs in on if "Die Hard" qualifies as a holiday movie.

item.title: S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative'
item.description: Rating agency S&P revised France’s outlook to "negative" from "stable" on Friday, citing growing budget pressures as weak economic growth and higher interest costs make it harder to reduce the deficit.

item.title: Kate in tears over her children's voice messages in cancer documentary
item.description: The Princess of Wales can be seen brushing away tears as she listens to voice messages from her children during her Three Peaks Challenge in a new documentary about her cancer battle.

item.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo
item.description: First, Uganda is heading for the exit in eastern DR Congo. Kampala has announced the withdrawal of its troops from a key town in North Kivu, as relations with Kinshasa deteriorate following provocative comments from Uganda's army chief. Then, pregnant women are struggling to cope with extreme heat, while health experts warn of growing risks for unborn babies, from dehydration to premature births. And, after seeking safety, opportunity and a better life, many migrants in South Africa now face hostility, violence and growing exclusion. As anti-immigration sentiment gains ground, the country's promise is fading for those who once saw it as a land of hope.

item.title: Millions clean up after massive Thanksgiving storms on East Coast
item.description: The East Coast is recovering from the massive Thanksgiving Day storms that flooded streets, toppled trees and left tens of thousands of homes without power.

item.title: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response
item.description: ⁠Ukraine ​made a Black Sea ceasefire offer ​to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked ​two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.

item.title: Spanish elections: 'Right-wing voters extremely mobilised, left-wing voters not mobilised enough'
item.description: “His main political platform is to say, I am not Sánchez, I am the opposite of Sánchez.” As Spain heads to the polls, what do Alberto Núñez Feijóo's campaign and political career tell us about the kind of prime minister he might become? Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Politics and Institutions Programme and lecturer at Sciences Po in Paris, joins Gavin Lee to break down the Popular Party leader's efforts to avoid the mistakes of 2023 and keep right-wing voters mobilised without galvanising the left.

item.title: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap
item.description: Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines. This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on? Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.

item.title: The AI revolution: Will I lose my job?
item.description: Have you heard of FOBO? It stands for fear of being obsolete. So as AI spreads, is it going to impact women in the workforce more than men? And are we right to be fearful of becoming obsolete? The International Labour Organization has already found occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to job losses thanks to generative AI, compared to those dominated by men.

item.title: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?
item.description: After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.

item.title: 'From bad to catastrophic: Iran's justice system was already unfair for many decades'
item.description: Amid war with the US and Israel, Iranian protesters continue to face death sentences following what Amnesty International describes as grossly unfair, torture-tainted trials. “The situation has changed from bad to catastrophic,” says Raha Bahreini, Iranian-Canadian human rights lawyer and Amnesty International's researcher on Iran. Bahreini discusses the aftermath of the January 2026 protests, the authorities' efforts to equate peaceful dissent with treason and espionage, and the extrajudicial killings of peaceful protesters. Amnesty International is calling for an international criminal justice mechanism, potentially a special tribunal. “There needs to be criminal accountability for these crimes against humanity.”

item.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row
item.description: Uganda's army on Friday said it planned to withdraw from the eastern DR Congo town of Lubero in North Kivu. The announcement came days after Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – son of President Yoweri Museveni – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, sparking a diplomatic spat between the two neighbouring nations.

item.title: Spain races to stop oil spill after ship capsizes off Ibiza
item.description: Spanish authorities raced to contain any damage to ecologically valuable Mediterranean waters on Thursday after a tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel capsized off Ibiza, leaving one dead.

item.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon demands ‘thorough overhaul’ of Germany ties
item.description: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party, on Friday declared he was "hostile" to German economic liberalism and its dominance of the European Union. The septuagenarian presidential candidate in the 2027 race also warned that France could be drawn into unwanted conflict as Germany's growing military strength makes it a "target" for other countries.

item.title: OM - Levski Sofia: A night of violence disrupts Marseille match
item.description: 🇫🇷 ⚽ 🇧🇬 At least 11 supporters of Bulgarian football club #LevskiSofia were injured in Marseille on Thursday, as skirmishes broke out between the visiting club and fans of hosts Olympique Marseille (#OM) before their Europa League fixture, FRANCE 24 has the details.

item.title: Paris Paloma tackles Greek mythology, generative AI in her second album 'The Fatal Flaw'
item.description: Dheepthika Laurent chats with Paris Paloma on set ahead of her Paris concert. The UK singer-songwriter and guitarist is promoting her second album, "The Fatal Flaw", an ode to Greek mythology, art and feminism. She tells us why this album is more personal than her first record, "Cacophony".

item.title: France is dealing with water insecurity – a new study shows it's a global problem
item.description: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. But this is a global problem, as a new study released Wednesday revealed "the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded" since 1991, when data collection began.

item.title: Big EU defence projects under threat from proposed budget cuts: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius
item.description: We speak to the EU's Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andrius Kubilius. The former prime minister of Lithuania – who grew up during the Soviet era – tells us how he sees the confrontation between Europe and Russia. He also sounds the alarm over proposed cuts in the EU's future budget, saying that they could jeopardise major European projects in defence and space. Kubilius praises the EU's SAFE defence loans programme, remarking that it has been "really very successful".

item.title: From cyberbullying to extremist content, can EU Kids Act protect minors online?
item.description: Almost every European teenager is online. Some 96 percent of 15-year-olds use social media, yet many say they do not feel safe there. One in four children in the EU, aged 12 to 17, report having experienced cyberbullying, and nearly one in three say social media has left them feeling stressed, sad or socially excluded.

item.title: Asia and Europe stocks rally after volatile week
item.description: Stocks jumped on Wall Street on Friday, putting markets on track for strong weekly gains despite several days of erratic swings. Jameel Ahmad, Chief Analyst at GTC, tells us more.

item.title: Turkey summons Georgian envoy after football fans' pro-Palestine protest sparks clashes
item.description: Turkey summoned ​Georgia's ambassador on ​Friday over violence that broke out ​at ‌a Europa ⁠League match in Batumi ‌between the Turkish Besiktas ⁠and Israeli Hapoel Beer-Sheva teams, according to a foreign ministry source. Clashes erupted after Besiktas fans unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during the match, sparking the diplomatic row.

item.title: Sierra Leone: Maternal deaths fall as healthcare improves, but challenges remain
item.description: Sierra Leone was once considered one of the most dangerous countries in the world to give birth. Maternal deaths have since fallen dramatically, thanks to improvements in healthcare, medical training and maternity services. But despite this progress, significant challenges remain. Activists warn that continued efforts are needed to ensure safer pregnancies and childbirth for women across the country. Clarisse Fortuné reports.

item.title: France: Macron lashes out at Le Pen’s ‘arrogance’
item.description: 🇫🇷 French President Emmanuel #Macron on Thursday responded to far-right leader and 2027 presidential candidate Marine #LePen’s claim that he was “blocking” the French people’s freedom of expression. Listen in to what he had to say.

item.title: DR Congo: Copper reserves put Africa at the centre of the global race for critical minerals
item.description: Africa is emerging as a key player in the global race for copper, accounting for around 10 per cent of the world's estimated reserves. The Democratic Republic of Congo is at the centre of this growing interest, having mined 3.4 million metric tons of copper in 2025. Its vast mineral resources are attracting growing attention from countries and companies around the world, as demand for the metal rises due to its importance in energy infrastructure, electric vehicles and the global transition to cleaner energy.

item.title: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?
item.description: Spanish women’s refusal to surrender hard-won rights helped Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez clinch an unlikely victory in a snap election three years ago. As he gambles with another early vote on Sunday, his hopes of defying the odds rest on women again rallying to block the far right from governing Spain for the first time since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship.

item.title: Sales for Biden memoir fall far short of books by Obama, Clinton
item.description: Former President Joe Biden’s memoir “Promise Me, America” has sold around 21,000 copies during its first week on sale, according to Circana, a firm which tracks the physical book sales market

item.title: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections
item.description: Political violence is escalating in Nigeria ahead of the general elections scheduled for January. Candidates and their supporters have increasingly come under attack, with armed groups disrupting campaign rallies and some assaults resulting in deaths. Despite the growing number of incidents, security forces have struggled to contain the violence. With less than two months to go before the vote, fears are mounting that intimidation and deadly attacks could prevent many Nigerians from freely taking part in the democratic process.

item.title: Body found in woodland confirmed as missing Kelsey Hunter
item.description: The body of a woman found in woodland in Scotland has been identified as 20-year-old Kelsey Hunter, who went missing over the weekend.

item.title: French student protests: A 'very bizarre' government response
item.description: “The government had a very bizarre way of dealing with the student protests,” says Jean-Rémi Girard, a secondary school teacher and union representative in Asnières-sur-Seine. He explains how teachers sought to defuse tensions by listening to students, and respecting their right to protest, while keeping classes running. He recounts a police intervention last October and the case of a student facing trial for defending a classmate, and has the full support of several teachers. Girard questions the government's heavy-handed policing and largely symbolic proposals on class sizes and university admissions. “There wasn't really a negotiation,” he says, also highlighting the number of education workers injured during the protests.
